LakeCat: A Thin, Governed, Replayable Catalog Foundation

Open Iceberg Interoperability, Apache Ossie Semantics, and Evidence-Bearing Evaluation

Alexy Khrabrov — QueryGraph Project

2026-08-28

Abstract

Open table formats have separated analytical data from individual query engines, but the catalog has become a consequential coordination boundary: it must preserve table-format semantics across heterogeneous clients while mediating identity, authorization, metadata-pointer transitions, recovery, lineage, and increasingly semantic models used by people and AI agents. This paper presents LakeCat, a Rust-native Apache Iceberg REST catalog foundation for QueryGraph. LakeCat deliberately keeps this boundary thin. It owns catalog identity, tenancy, optimistic metadata-pointer state, idempotency, policy gates, audit, and a transactional outbox; it delegates reusable Iceberg interpretation to Sail, governance semantics to TypeSec, graph behavior to Grust, and end-to-end composition to QueryGraph. We further describe an Apache Ossie supply chain in which immutable semantic artifacts are structurally and physically validated, policy-bound, compare-and-swap published, projected, and correlated with OpenLineage evidence before an answer is admitted. Evaluation uses catalog-bench, a source-pinned, non-ranking behavioral harness. Stock Spark, Flink, Trino, and DuckDB clients execute a common 14-assertion Iceberg workload against LakeCat, Apache Polaris, Apache Gravitino, and Lakekeeper. Additional campaigns exercise ambiguous commits, service restart, cold restore, peer migration, HadoopCatalog registration, outbox recovery, and Ossie-backed TPC-DS semantic drift. The results show protocol interoperability across the four catalogs and demonstrate that correctness evidence can extend beyond the immediate REST response without placing non-standard metadata in Iceberg tables. The paper reports correctness and recovery observations, not a throughput ranking or a compliant TPC-DS performance result.
